guide.about: Rug Gallery sells hand-knotted Persian rugs and modern designs. Delivery is free anywhere in the EU, usually within 5 to 10 working days. Any design can be made to measure on request. Use Enquire on a piece and the shop will reply within a day.
guide.greeting: Welcome to Rug Gallery! I'm Ava. Have a look around, or shall I show you round?
guide.name: Ava

tour.intro: Lovely, let's begin. Come with me to the front desk, where every visit starts.
tour.say: This is our reception. If you would like a rug sent out on approval, or a piece made to your own measurements, this is where we arrange it. Delivery anywhere in the EU is free.
tour.title: Reception

tour.intro: First, the runners. We lay them out on the tables so you can see them up close.
tour.say: Here is the Heriz runner. See how the brick red border frames the teal field. That is an old Heriz trick for hiding everyday wear, and its twin lies on the table across the lobby.
Beside it, the Tabriz, much softer in cream and pale gold. Look closely at the florals: there are about a hundred and twenty thousand knots in every square metre.

tour.intro: Now through to the main hall. It opens up the moment you step inside.
tour.say: This is the Woven Spiral, the heart of the hall. It isn't for sale, I'm afraid, but it shows how a single thread becomes a structure. Every rug in this room began the same way.
tour.title: The Woven Spiral

tour.say: Just to our right, the Mahal. Its florals are open and relaxed rather than crowded, and the rust comes from vegetable dyes, so it mellows beautifully over the years.

tour.intro: Let's walk the east wall, from the simplest weave to the finest.
tour.say: We begin with the Farmhouse border rug in navy and cream, flat-woven and fully reversible. It's the easiest piece here to live with, and at €540, the gentlest on the wallet.
The Motion wall rug takes our brushstroke design and sizes it for a wall. Stand back a step and the bands of faded denim almost seem to move.
And here, the Isfahan: wool and silk together, hand-knotted in Iran. Catch it at an angle and the silk lifts the ivory with a quiet sheen. It comes with a batten, ready to hang.

tour.intro: Round the corner now, to the north wall.
tour.say: The Farmhouse stripe is woven on a hand loom in Portugal from undyed wool. Look at the edges: they are whipped by hand, which is why they lie so flat. Its pair hangs at the far end of this wall.
Next to it, the marine wave. The same family as the Motion denim, but cooler and calmer, with flecks of sand running through the blue.

tour.intro: Let's step in among the plinths. These are the floor rugs, laid flat, the way you would live with them.
tour.say: The Vinton in teal is our classic medallion. New Zealand wool gives it that soft, low pile, and the fringes are finished by hand.
Its sister, the Vinton in rust, is washed after weaving for an antique, lived-in look. People often take it for a much older rug.
The Motion in marine is the one I suggest for open rooms. The pile is dense, so it softens echoes as well as footsteps.
And the Motion in denim, with those loose brushstroke bands. It's tufted in India on a cotton backing, and light enough to move from room to room.

tour.intro: Across to the west wall, where three favourites hang side by side.
tour.say: This is the easiest wall for comparing. The marine wave, the Mahal and the Isfahan hang together, so you can see a modern tufted weave right beside two hand-knotted ones.
tour.title: The west wall

tour.intro: And now, the piece I've saved for last.
tour.say: This is our Kashan Heirloom, hand-knotted around forty years ago in rust, indigo and ivory, and carefully restored. Step closer and you'll see where the colours have softened with age. It's €8,900, and it's the one rug here I would never tire of.
